summary: Deployed a rootless podman container as unprivileged user appsvc on node1 (RHEL7), serving on port 8080 via a boot-enabled systemd system service, requiring no login session for appsvc. Verified persistence and recovery across a full node restart.
actions_performed: Cleared a stale yum.pid lock and enabled the rhel-7-server-extras-rpms channel to install podman 1.6.4, runc, conmon, slirp4netns, and fuse-overlayfs
Set user.max_user_namespaces=28633 via /etc/sysctl.d/99-podman-userns.conf (was 0, which blocked all rootless containers) and applied it live
Created unprivileged system account appsvc (nologin shell) with subuid/subgid ranges 200000:65536 in /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid

Added /etc/tmpfiles.d/appsvc-runtime.conf to persistently create /run/user/997 (appsvc's XDG_RUNTIME_DIR) at boot via systemd-tmpfiles-setup.service, since this RHEL7 systemd build ships no user@.service template, so systemctl --user / loginctl linger cannot be used to start services

Diagnosed and fixed a rootless podman EPERM/chdir failure caused by an inherited working directory appsvc's user namespace could not access; fixed by always invoking podman with an accessible WorkingDirectory

Pulled docker.io/library/python:alpine and built a systemd system unit /etc/systemd/system/appsvc-webapp.service (Type=oneshot, RemainAfterExit=yes) that runs podman run as User=appsvc/Group=appsvc, publishing container port 8080 to host port 8080 and serving a static page from /home/appsvc/webroot
Enabled and started the unit; verified HTTP 200 on $NODE_IP:8080 and that conmon/python processes run under uid appsvc, with zero active login sessions for appsvc

Captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, service/container state, HTTP 200), restarted node1 via reboot with the acknowledgement returned before disconnection, polled until SSH access returned (about 2 hours later), confirmed boot_id changed, and reverified the service was enabled/active, the container running, HTTP 200, and no login session for appsvc

evidence.requirement: Containerized web app runs as unprivileged account appsvc on port 8080
evidence.summary: podman ps shows webapp container up with 0.0.0.0:8080->8080/tcp; ps output shows conmon and python3 http.server processes owned by user appsvc; curl to $NODE_IP:8080 returns HTTP 200 with the served page

evidence.requirement: Service starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
evidence.summary: systemd system unit appsvc-webapp.service (Type=oneshot/RemainAfterExit, User=appsvc) created and enabled for multi-user.target; loginctl list-sessions shows no session for appsvc, only unrelated antrieb sessions

evidence.requirement: Rootless container prerequisites (user namespaces, subuid/subgid, podman) correctly configured
evidence.summary: user.max_user_namespaces raised from 0 to 28633 via persistent sysctl.d file; appsvc created with subuid/subgid 200000:65536; podman 1.6.4 installed from RHEL7 extras channel

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before node restart
evidence.summary: Pre-restart baseline: boot_id 151c4aa9-9e81-4a32-9c22-08c5c441403a, service active+enabled, container Up, HTTP 200, zero login sessions for appsvc

evidence.requirement: Node restarted one at a time using native safe reboot, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Issued `sudo reboot` backgrounded with a short delay so the exec call's acknowledgement returned before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart (not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id 9f9c65b8-099c-4af1-a7e3-29f09c2eec47 differs from the pre-restart boot_id, confirming an actual kernel restart occurred, not just a service bounce

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required service, container, data, and appsvc login-session-free state
evidence.summary: After restart: appsvc-webapp.service active+enabled and auto-started the container at boot; podman ps shows webapp Up; curl returns HTTP 200 with the same served content; conmon/python processes owned by appsvc; loginctl shows no appsvc session; subuid/subgid, tmpfiles rule, and unit enablement all persisted across reboot
